ov: The leafy seadragon, a relative of the seahorse covered in leaf-like lobes of skin that make it look like floating seaweed. It lives only off the southern and western coasts of Australia and is the marine emblem of South Australia.
rg: Southern Australian waters, from Wilson’s Promontory in Victoria west to Jurien Bay in Western Australia.
df: Small crustaceans such as amphipods and mysid shrimp, plankton and larval fish, sucked up through its pipe-like snout.
fx: As with seahorses, the male carries the eggs: up to 250, stuck to a brood patch under his tail for about nine weeks.
Only about 5% of the eggs survive to become adults.
